slides.title: Gossip Agents: Reputation through Opinion Dynamics over Evolving Networks
slides.highlight: This work explores how reputational information propagates through dynamic communication networks using opinion dynamics, offering insights into the emergence of cooperation in hybrid human-AI societies relevant to MIMIC's societal-scale simulation goals.

card.one_liner: Gossip-based reputation diffusion via DeGroot dynamics promotes cooperation in dynamic multi-agent networks.
card.key_idea: Agents form private opinions from observations, exchange them via DeGroot averaging over evolving networks, and aggregate them into reputation signals.
card.evaluation: Tested in n-player Prisoner's Dilemma and Harvest gridworlds against no-reputation baselines, measuring cooperation, utility, sustainability, and peacefulness.
card.limitation: Relies on fixed, hand-designed assessment rules for prosocial/antisocial behavior, which may not generalize to complex real-world environments.

slides.title: Towards Adaptive and Real-Survey-Aligned Simulated Urban Mobility Behaviour of Generative Agents
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates how generative agents built on large language models can simulate complex, adaptive multimodal urban mobility behaviors, offering a method to align agent decisions with real household travel surveys.

card.one_liner: Generative agents match survey modal splits but fail individual trip accuracy, though they adapt to unforeseen events.
card.key_idea: Compares LLM-based generative agents against discrete choice models in urban mobility simulations, testing prompt tuning and memory mechanisms.
card.evaluation: Assessed on 3,299 trips from a Toulouse household survey using 15 decision-makers, measuring modal split divergence and trip-level accuracy.
card.limitation: Generative agents achieve realistic aggregate modal splits but significantly lower individual trip accuracy compared to fitted statistical models.

slides.title: GCAM-Gym: A Benchmark for Agent-Based Climate Policy Search
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a standardized environment for evaluating agent-based climate policy search methods, offering insights into how autonomous agents can navigate complex societal and environmental feedback loops relevant to MIMIC's focus on multi-scale societal simulation.

card.one_liner: GCAM-Gym benchmarks agent-based climate policy search, showing CMA-ES outperforms other methods in finding cost-effective policies.
card.key_idea: A Gymnasium-compatible interface for GCAM supporting full-policy and stepwise control, comparing seven search systems on target attainment, cost, and delayed feedback.
card.evaluation: Compared seven systems (e.g., CMA-ES, BO, PPO) over 3,210 GCAM evaluations using IQM metrics; results are trustworthy but constrained by simulator runtime defects.
card.limitation: Runtime diagnostics revealed state-mutating errors affecting temperature readings, requiring new evaluations under a qualified runtime to validate policy outcomes and rankings.

slides.title: Context Matters! Social, Spatial, and Semantic Coordination with an Embodied Agent in Immersive Analytics
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for designing embodied AI agents in AR that coordinate via spatial, social, and semantic context, relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Proposes a spatial, social, and semantic context framework for embodied AI agents in immersive analytics.
card.key_idea: Defines context via embeddedness and awareness across spatial, social, and semantic dimensions; implemented in Cobot, an AR agent using LLMs and gaze cues.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a reflective design case study (Cobot) and hypothetical use scenarios; lacks empirical user studies or quantitative metrics.
card.limitation: Framework is preliminary and single-user focused; relies on informal testing without rigorous validation of design factors.

slides.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
slides.highlight: This work introduces a method for sensitivity analysis in agent-based models with hierarchical decision structures, addressing the limitations of classical approaches on branched parameter spaces. It is relevant to MIMIC for improving the interpretability of agent decision-making processes in complex societal simulations.

card.one_liner: A novel sensitivity analysis method for agent-based models with hierarchical, conditionally active decision parameters.
card.key_idea: Combines random forest supervision with HSIC-ANOVA on a hierarchical design space to rank main effects and interactions without imputing inactive variables.
card.evaluation: Applied to MAELIA agro-ecological model (5,000 simulations) for nitrogen leaching, carbon variation, and yield; validated against classical GSA limitations.
card.limitation: Requires computationally intensive surrogate training and assumes the hierarchical structure of decisions is correctly specified by experts.

slides.title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design
slides.tldr: LIMITED PERSONALITY TRANSFER VIA VOICE CLONING
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that cloning familiar voices does not systematically transfer personality impressions to virtual characters, challenging assumptions about voice-based social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Cloning familiar voices for virtual characters yields limited personality transfer, primarily activating identity expectations rather than reconstructing person impressions.
card.key_idea: Two within-subject studies compared character ratings using cloned known-voice versus unknown-voice, measuring alignment with memory-based ratings of the original speaker.
card.evaluation: Study 1 (n=17, lecturer) and Study 2 (n=65, creators) used Big Five and social scales; results showed only selective, non-replicable trait effects.
card.limitation: Small samples, brief stimuli, and German-speaking contexts limit generalizability; effects may differ for closer relationships or longer interactions.

slides.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
slides.tldr: Mental World Model for Dynamic ToM
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Mental World Model framework that explicitly constructs subjective worlds and simulates continuous mental evolution, offering a mechanism for dynamic Theory of Mind inference that aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates inferring partners' intent and self-monitoring via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: Mental World Model framework simulates subjective cognition evolution, outperforming LLMs in Theory of Mind tasks.
card.key_idea: MWM/MMEA explicitly constructs subjective worlds, models cognition-mental state interactions, and simulates continuous mental evolution via historical dependencies.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DynToM/RecToM (96.48%/94.00% accuracy) and prediction tasks, outperforming leading LLMs and specialized ToM methods.

slides.title: YYForce Brings Humanoid Robots to Hospitality in Landmark Partnership with Novotel & Mercure Singapore on Stevens
slides.highlight: The deployment of humanoid robots in hospitality settings offers practical insights into human-robot interaction and social engagement in public spaces, relevant to the development of embodied social robots.

slides.title: Anthropic Unveils Next-Gen Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture
slides.highlight: Anthropic's new architecture enables Claude to generate self-written programs for managing AI agents, offering a scalable approach to multi-agent orchestration relevant to modeling complex hybrid human-AI societies.

slides.title: EarlyCommit: Calibrated Word-by-Word Commitment for Robots Acting Before You Finish Speaking
slides.tldr: EARLY ROBOT ACTION VIA WORD-BY-WORD CALIBRATION
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a method for robots to act on partial speech by calibrating word-by-word object commitment, which aligns with HyECHO's goal of modeling real-time human-AI interaction dynamics and listener engagement.

card.one_liner: Robots act on partial speech via calibrated word-by-word object commitment, reducing latency while controlling error risk.
card.key_idea: Fine-tuned text encoder scores scene objects per word; temperature calibration enables a threshold-based commit/wait/ask decision rule.
card.evaluation: Synthetic tabletop scenes with unseen words; 92% accuracy at τ=0.9, 1.6-2x more commits than keyword matching, 31-35ms/word.
card.limitation: Relies on templated instructions and small vocabularies; lacks physical robot validation, user studies, and finite-sample safety guarantees.

slides.title: Iterative Design and Evaluation of a VR Nursing Training System
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates how iterative VR design can enhance procedural skill acquisition and clinical decision-making, offering insights relevant to MOSAIC's focus on skill estimation and adaptive coaching in complex tasks.

card.one_liner: Iteratively designed VR nursing system improves student confidence and procedural skills via expert-guided refinements.
card.key_idea: Collaborative VR development with nursing specialists, using finite state machines for clinical scenarios and iterative user feedback to refine UI and fidelity.
card.evaluation: Two mixed-methods studies (n=8 experts, n=17 students) using SSQ, UAQ, and CCEI-C; showed high acceptance and confidence gains, though sample sizes are small.
card.limitation: Small sample sizes limit generalizability; lacks haptic feedback for psychomotor skills; relies on self-reported metrics rather than objective clinical performance.

slides.title: Moss Intelligence raises $149M Pre-A for real-time multimodal AI
slides.highlight: Moss Intelligence raised $149M in a Pre-A round to advance real-time multimodal AI, a capability relevant to HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception.

slides.title: Do You Trust It... or Check It?: Exploring Children's Verification Behaviors in Game-Based Human-AI Collaboration
slides.tldr: CHILDREN'S VERIFICATION BEHAVIORS IN AI COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This study examines how children verify AI suggestions through situated behaviors like evidence checking and questioning, offering insights into human-AI interaction dynamics relevant to MOSAIC's focus on aligning human proficiency with AI assistance.

card.one_liner: Game-based study reveals children's AI verification behaviors vary by agent interaction style.
card.key_idea: Embeds partially correct AI suggestions in a biology game, comparing partner-like, tool-like, and dynamic agent styles to observe situated verification behaviors.
card.evaluation: Preliminary study with 12 children (ages 8-10) using interaction logs, post-task ratings, and interviews; small sample limits statistical power.
card.limitation: Extremely small sample size (n=12) prevents causal conclusions; trust model relies on observable behaviors rather than internal states.

slides.title: Choosing LLMs for Strategic Agent Interactions
slides.highlight: This work addresses strategic model selection in adversarial settings, relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of adaptive AI teammates that infer partner intent and self-correct during dynamic human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Formalizes LLM selection as a strategic meta-game, showing bandits outperform routers against adaptive opponents.
card.key_idea: Treats model selection as a repeated meta-game where a selector fields LLMs against unknown, adaptive opponents using online feedback.
card.evaluation: Tested 10 LLMs across 5 games; Thompson Sampling bandits outperformed embedding-based routers and LLM reflection methods.
card.limitation: Selectors fail to beat best fixed models; non-stationary bandit variants underperform stationary baselines against adaptive opponents.

slides.title: CF-AVSS: A Coarse-to-Fine Audio-Visual Speech Separation Framework with Target-Speaker Refinement and Post-Fusion for Real-World AVSE Challenge
slides.highlight: This work presents a two-stage audio-visual speech enhancement framework that effectively separates target speech from overlapping speakers and noise, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust diarization and addressee modeling in complex acoustic environments.

card.one_liner: Two-stage coarse-to-fine AVSE framework achieves top rankings and lowest CER in real-world challenges.
card.key_idea: Progressive visually-conditioned separation preserves context, followed by TFGridNet refinement and calibrated linear post-fusion.
card.evaluation: ISCSLP 2026 Challenge (Tracks 1/2) using SI-SDR, PESQ, CER, and OVRL; tied 1st/2nd with best CER.
card.limitation: Relies on synchronized visual cues, which degrade under occlusion, blur, or desynchronization in Track 2.

slides.title: Think Once, Reflect Twice: How Feedback Shapes Human-AI Collaboration
slides.highlight: This study examines how feedback interventions influence human reflection and reliance behavior in human-AI teams, offering insights relevant to modeling engagement and group norms in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Feedback on past AI overrides triggers retrospective reflection but risks reducing concurrent reasoning.
card.key_idea: Behavioral study testing feedback on successful/unsuccessful AI overrides to induce reflection-on-action and calibrate reliance.
card.evaluation: N=244 loan approval task; ANCOVA on reflection/reliance metrics; mixed-methods with qualitative thematic analysis.
card.limitation: Unidirectional feedback may suppress reflection-in-action; performance gains are context-dependent and not universally observed.

slides.title: Reliable Knowledge Acquisition for Continual Learning Agents
slides.highlight: This work addresses the challenge of filtering unreliable memories in continual learning agents, a critical requirement for ADAM-CHAT's goal of robust self-correction and adaptive knowledge reuse in open-ended environments.

card.one_liner: RIKA improves continual learning by hierarchically extracting and evidence-gating reliable knowledge from agent trajectories.
card.key_idea: Combines hierarchical extraction of four knowledge types with Evidence-based Knowledge Admission to filter harmful claims using sequential hypothesis testing.
card.evaluation: Tested on six Continual Learning Bench streams with four LLM backbones; RIKA achieved highest aggregate scores, outperforming baselines like Mem0 and ACE.
card.limitation: Evaluated only on text-based, tool-mediated tasks with fixed model parameters; transferability to perceptual or physical environments remains unverified.

slides.title: A humanoid robot for education costs $299. Its curriculum is $499.
slides.highlight: The availability of low-cost humanoid robots for education highlights the growing accessibility of embodied learning tools, a key area of interest for social robotics research.

slides.title: Technology-Supported Moderation in Online Deliberation
slides.highlight: The Stanford Online Deliberation Platform demonstrates automated moderation and speaker management for small groups, offering insights relevant to HyECHO's goal of modeling group norms and engagement in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Stanford's platform enables scalable, automated online deliberation for mini-publics, reducing costs while maintaining parity with in-person outcomes.
card.key_idea: Browser-based platform for small synchronous groups uses structured agendas, automated moderation, and speaking nudges to replace human facilitators.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 54 large-scale deliberations (30k+ participants); RCTs confirm opinion shifts and satisfaction match in-person benchmarks.
card.limitation: Lacks informal social bonding, potentially excludes low-tech-literacy users, and risks attendance volatility due to lower commitment barriers.

slides.title: Behavioural Sociology of Humans and Machines
slides.highlight: This chapter examines how social categorization, reciprocity, and authority mechanisms shift in human-machine interactions, providing a sociological lens for understanding the collective dynamics and norms within hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Review of how AI participation reshapes social mechanisms like categorization, reciprocity, and authority in hybrid intelligence.
card.key_idea: Analyzes sociological processes in human-machine interaction, focusing on altered mechanisms of social perception, cooperation, and institutional arrangements.
card.evaluation: Qualitative literature review synthesizing insights from sociology, HCI, and organizational studies; no empirical data or quantitative metrics presented.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation, relying on theoretical synthesis; distinguishes established findings from speculative long-term consequences without concrete evidence.

slides.title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers
slides.highlight: This work introduces SPLIT, a method for optimally allocating test-time compute between sampling and verification under imperfect verifiers, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of adaptive AI teammates that efficiently manage inference resources and self-correct via meta-cognitive verification.

card.one_liner: SPLIT allocates test-time compute near-optimally by modeling imperfect verifier errors and correlations.
card.key_idea: Derives exact success formulas for verifier selection, estimates parameters via empirical Bayes on pilots, and optimizes budget allocation.
card.evaluation: Tested on 7 benchmarks, 26 models, and 175 agents; achieves 0.02–0.8% regret vs. oracle, outperforming fixed rules by >2.5%.
card.limitation: Requires a labeled pilot dataset for calibration; performance depends on accurate estimation of verifier error correlations.

slides.title: Sub-Millisecond Reflexes for Continuous Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work introduces a sub-millisecond reflex engine for ROS 2 that enables deterministic control switching and safety mitigations, directly supporting the low-latency responsiveness required for safe embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Open-source ROS 2 framework enables sub-millisecond controller switching for uninterrupted, safe human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Enhanced multimode controller uses lock-free pointer swaps and pre-allocated resources to eliminate runtime middleware overhead during control transitions.
card.evaluation: Validated on Franka Panda; achieved <0.1ms switching latency, 3.5% faster task completion, and 3x lower jerk versus standard ros2_control baselines.
card.limitation: Reflex behaviors and safety thresholds are predefined and application-dependent, requiring careful manual tuning for specific tasks.
